solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An emphasis at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of the two words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A question about stressing something while on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' both scrambles AN EMPHASIS and, read as a whole, points to the skill of sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in handling a ship is what you would stress when out on the ocean, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Rifle fire

definitions.meaning: to rifle a place is to plunder or ransack it
to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to plunder a captured town, and to dismiss an employee.

clue.text: Article, quite new — not this then?

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of quite are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone describing an item as fairly recent, then doubting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points back to the word 'new': something old and valuable is precisely not new.
explanation.definitionFit: An old collectable piece is the opposite of new, so it is what 'not new' describes.

clue.text: Diane's put in a welcome bid, so end unresolved argument amicably

parts.note: to welcome someone is to greet them

indicators.note: put in signals that one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a bid is an offer
Di is a short form of the name Diane; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Diane makes a friendly offer to settle a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diane's' looks like the subject of the sentence; only DI (her short name) is used, and the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to accept that a disagreement will not be resolved and stay on good terms.

clue.text: Disreputable son, good-for-nothing pocketing Ecstasy

indicators.note: pocketing means taking something into a pocket, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a good-for-nothing person is idle and lazy
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A wayward son, a layabout, caught carrying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' puts E inside LAZY to give LEAZY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sordid and of bad repute is described as seedy or disreputable.

clue.text: Male after one on phone still

indicators.note: after places the male letter following the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
being on the mobile means using a phone

explanation.surface: A man calling someone after the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and motionless are synonyms: not moving at all.

clue.text: Male part shortened

indicators.note: shortened signals that the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a stage is a part or phase of a process

explanation.surface: A section of something that has been cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is called by this name, as is a man at a pre-wedding party.

clue.text: SI unit spelt differently — ampere, initially, in this country

indicators.note: spelt differently means the letters are rearranged into another word
initially picks the first letter of ampere

explanation.surface: A scientific note about the ampere being an SI unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelt differently' rearranges SIUNIT into TUNISI, and the ampere is genuinely an SI unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African republic is the country in question.

clue.text: Novelist in danger, goes abroad

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer in peril heads overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of the nineteenth-century French writer Aurore Dupin.

clue.text: Group from Great Lake bed shown first

indicators.note: shown first puts the bed before the lake

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A party drawn from a lake, with a bed displayed ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A small exclusive circle of people is a clique or group.

clue.text: Souvenir from Rome, men took

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Tourists picked up a keepsake on a trip to Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake kept to remember a place or event is a souvenir.

clue.text: By implication, glibness — it has advantages and disadvantages

parts.note: read as an instruction, mix the letters of the second word of the answer and you get this clue word

explanation.surface: Smooth talk is said to bring both good and bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By implication' warns that the answer read as wordplay (an anagram signal followed by its fodder) gives the clue word glibness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names something welcome that also brings drawbacks.

clue.text: Clutch case for concertina

parts.note: to clutch is to squeeze
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A grip and a container stand in for a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezebox is an informal name for a concertina or accordion.

clue.text: Decline to show epic that appears endless

indicators.note: that appears endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a saga is a long epic story

explanation.surface: Turning down a film that seems to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'epic that appears endless' sounds like a long film; it is SAGA cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or decline, as prices do.

clue.text: Happy chappie produces a flag

parts.note: jolly means happy
Roger stands for any man's name, a chappie

explanation.surface: A cheerful fellow brings out a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones pirate flag has this name.

clue.text: Cat in patch of ground by old church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lot is a plot of land

explanation.surface: A cat seen in a field beside an ancient church.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-sized spotted wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Jokes about stableman, last to wear best clothes

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jokes surround the other pieces

parts.note: gags are jokes
a lad is a stable worker who looks after horses

indicators.note: last to picks the final letter of wear

explanation.surface: Humour about a groom, who is the last to dress up.
explanation.walkthrough: A lad is the British word for a stable worker who looks after racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's smartest party outfit.

clue.text: Black passenger ship and plane

parts.note: jet black is a deep black
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A dark ocean vessel and an aircraft listed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet-powered passenger aircraft is a plane.

clue.text: Legislator in Volksraad originally appearing in real wig, plaited

indicators.note: appearing in puts one piece inside another
plaited means woven together, so the letters are interlaced into a new order
originally picks the first letter of Volksraad

explanation.surface: A lawmaker in the old Boer parliament wearing a braided wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plaited' rearranges REAL WIG into LAWGIER and 'appearing in' sets V within it. The Volksraad was the parliament of the Boer republics.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gives laws to a people is a legislator.

clue.text: Sweet plonk plonker knocked over

parts.note: plonk is slang for cheap wine

indicators.note: knocked over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: plonker is British slang for a fool, a mug

explanation.surface: Cheap wine spilled by a clumsy idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets plonk next to plonker; one is wine, the other a fool (MUG). A wine gum is a chewy British sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine gum is a chewy fruit-flavoured confectionery, so a sweet.

clue.text: Young cow back on bottle

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a calf is a young cow

explanation.surface: A calf returns to a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A flacon is a small stoppered bottle, especially for scent.

clue.text: Statesman left in style after start of convention

indicators.note: after places the other pieces following that first letter
start of picks the first letter of convention

parts.note: taken as written
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A politician departing in fine style after a party gathering opens.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton, US president, is a statesman.

clue.text: Robbery claim raised

parts.note: to hold is to claim or maintain an opinion
up means raised

explanation.surface: An assertion is lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is an armed robbery.

clue.text: Ladder having last two of steps missing

indicators.note: last two of names the final pair of letters as the part removed
missing means those letters are absent

parts.note: rungs are the steps of a ladder

explanation.surface: A ladder lacking its top rungs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladder' looks like the climbing thing; it is the definition in the sense of a tear in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder in stockings or tights is also called a run.

clue.text: Do the same as someone else and pay close attention to businessman

definitions.text: Do the same as someone else

parts.note: to follow something is to watch it closely
a suit is slang for a business executive

explanation.surface: Copying someone while watching a businessman carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from card games, where you play the same suit as the leader.

clue.text: Piece of music filed away by librarian

indicators.note: filed away by means stored inside, so the letters are tucked in the word that follows

explanation.surface: A librarian stores a score in the archive.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera, a piece of music.

clue.text: Slightly mad king accompanied by popular cosmonaut

parts.note: gaga means a bit crazy or senile
R is the abbreviation for king, from Rex
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An eccentric ruler goes along with a famous space traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin was the first human in space, a Soviet cosmonaut.

clue.text: Itinerant type in fishing boat

definitions.meaning: a person who wanders from place to place without settling
a boat that fishes with a drift net

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an aimless wanderer and a fishing vessel using drift nets.

clue.text: Meat and drink to head of programming

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of programming

explanation.surface: Food and drink provided to a programme director.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump is a cut of beef from the hindquarters, so meat.

clue.text: Publicity material has right look, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said out loud, so what is heard matters

parts.note: right means proper and a look is a gander, informal British slang for a glance

explanation.surface: Promotional literature having the correct appearance, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: Having a gander is British slang for taking a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased information spread to promote a cause.
